subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept requester-owned outbound-only per-agent A2A allowlists as the public config contract, or require target-side receive/per-capability policy before landing this PR?
rationale: The PR changes cross-agent session authorization and adds a public config surface, so automation cannot choose the long-term security boundary or product contract safely.

options.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
options.body: Accept requester-owned semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, branch refresh, and focused validation before merge.

options.title: Require broader authorization first
options.body: Pause this branch and fold the work into a bidirectional or per-capability session authorization design before exposing new config.

options.title: Keep as discussion only
options.body: Leave the PR open for product discussion but do not land a public config contract until the broader per-agent scoping issue is resolved.

recommendation.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
recommendation.body: Accept requester-owned semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, branch refresh, and focused validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history covers the shared session visibility helper lineage and they are the strongest available owner for the authorization-contract choice.
